gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Valve's 2024-08-19 Counter-Strike 2 post "Side-stepping Skill" kicks players from Valve Official Servers for hardware input automation and tells owners of keyboards with "Snap Tap Mode" to disable it before a match, while rapid trigger is a different mechanism: a per-key reset by travel distance that Wooting offers down to 0.1 mm.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com/blog/best-gaming-keyboards-under-100 (cited), hlplanet.com/keyboards-hall-effect-switches (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net/best-budget-hall-effect-keyboard (cited), gamepadsquire.com (cited) and setupinsider.com. mkbguide already says "Some games limit SOCD-style features in competitive modes, so check the rules of the titles you play", and mechanicalkeyboard.net says to leave SOCD controls off "until you know what the server or tournament permits". Neither names the game, Valve's post, its date or the penalty (a kick from the match), and hlplanet, gamepadsquire and setupinsider list Snap Tap only as a feature. So rivals have the warning but not the rule. The other mechanism facts are also partly covered: gamepadsquire states the AULA F75 HE's 2.4 GHz mode "tops out at 1,000Hz — the 8K figure is wired-only", mkbguide states 8,000 Hz over USB and 2.4 GHz with Bluetooth at 125 Hz for the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR, mechanicalkeyboard.net states 8,000 Hz is one report every 0.125 ms, and mkbguide mentions north-pole-down switches. No rival page states whether rapid trigger itself keeps working on 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth, and none sets the budget boards' 0.005 mm step against Wooting's 0.1 mm.
decides: It does not change which board wins; it changes which feature the page should weigh. Every candidate advertises Snap Tap or SOCD alongside rapid trigger, and ChatGPT called its picks good "especially [for] Valorant and CS2". On Valve Official Servers the Snap Tap half must be switched off, so a CS2 buyer should choose on rapid trigger, polling by connection mode and layout. For our rows, Gamakay's TK75HE V2 page gives one 8 kHz polling figure with no per-mode split and claims "0.06ms wired and 2.4G wireless"; its "0.005mm" step is the maker's figure and is 20 times finer than the 0.1 mm Wooting offers. The TK75HE V2 takes N-pole magnetic switches only, which matters to anyone planning to swap switches.

findings.label: Valve's rule on hardware input automation in Counter-Strike 2
findings.value: "We are no longer going to allow automation (via scripting or hardware) that circumvent these core skills"
findings.note: Read through Steam's news API; the item's own URL is https://steamstore-a.akamaihd.net/news/externalpost/steam_community_announcements/6909171012611543335. Only this sentence is verbatim; the fetch tool returned the rest as a summary. The post is from 2024 and I did not open a 2026 Valve page confirming it still applies.

findings.label: Penalty and scope of Valve's rule
findings.value: On Valve Official Servers, players suspected of automating multiple actions from a single input may be kicked from their match; binds with more than one movement or attack action (null binds, jump-throw binds) no longer work; keyboards with an input-automation feature such as "Snap Tap Mode" should have it disabled before joining a match
findings.note: Paraphrase of the post as the tool summarised it, apart from the term "Snap Tap Mode". The summary names Snap Tap and binds and does not mention rapid trigger. Re-open the post to take exact wording before quoting on the page.

findings.label: How rapid trigger works, in Wooting's words
findings.value: "dynamically activating and deactivating the key based on travel distance instead of a fixed point in the key travel"
findings.note: Wooting is not an under-$100 candidate; cited as the maker that explains the feature. The page does not say whether games must support it and does not mention SOCD.

findings.label: Rapid trigger sensitivity Wooting offers
findings.note: For scale against the budget boards' maker figures: 0.1 mm ÷ 0.005 mm = 20 times coarser than Gamakay's stated step. Both are maker figures, not measurements.

findings.label: Polling and scan rate as the maker states them
findings.value: "8 KHz polling rate + 10 KHz scanning rate"; no separate figure per connection mode
findings.source_title: Gamakay TK75HE V2 Hall Effect keyboard 8K Polling Rate 0.005mm RT Accuracy
findings.note: Arithmetic: 10,000 scans/s is one scan every 0.1 ms; 8,000 reports/s is one report every 0.125 ms. The page does not state a Bluetooth polling rate or say whether rapid trigger works in wireless modes.

findings.source_title: Gamakay TK75HE V2 Hall Effect keyboard 8K Polling Rate 0.005mm RT Accuracy

findings.note: Maker figure. The page gives the rapid trigger range as 0.005–3.5 mm in one place and actuation as 0.005–3.7 mm in another.
